title: The Great Barrier Reef
text: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands stretching for over 2,300 km along the northeast coast of Australia in the Coral Sea. It is the largest living structure on Earth, visible from outer space. The reef supports extraordinary biodiversity, including more than 1,500 species of fish, 4,000 species of mollusk, and 240 species of birds. It was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981. The Great Barrier Reef faces significant threats from climate change, including coral bleaching caused by elevated sea temperatures, as well as water pollution and coastal development.
